Subject: Post-call: data retention expectations for PII-sensitive use case

Hi Camila --

Thanks for walking us through Redwood's hosting options earlier today. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can move to procurement:

- We're evaluating Redwood for a customer-facing feature that will process customer PII (names, phone numbers).
- Our security team requires either: 0-content retention (no stored request/response content) OR a very short, auditable retention window for logs (max 30 days) with strict access controls.
- We also need clarification on log contents - specifically whether prompts and model outputs are included in any runtime logs or only metadata (timestamps, request IDs, latency).

Can Redwood commit to a custom retention schedule for our account? If not on hosted, what are the options for Dedicated or Private to meet 0-retention or 30-day logs? Please include any required add-ons or pricing delta. Also, please share SOC2 or similar artifacts we can use with procurement.

Attaching a short summary of compliance questions the procurement team will use.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Johnson
Head of Product Security | Acme Corp

Subject: Re: Post-call: data retention expectations for PII-sensitive use case

Sara --

Appreciate the clear summary and the questions. Quick answers and proposed next steps: 

1) Retention options: Hosted API by default retains request/response content for 30 days for troubleshooting and abuse detection, but we can offer account-level retention policies. For strict 0-content retention we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment where we can disable persistent storage of request/response payloads entirely.

2) Logs: Runtime logs include request/response IDs, timestamps, and routing metadata by default. By policy we can exclude full prompts/outputs from long-term logs; short-term ephemeral caches may contain them purely for inference and are not written to persistent logs unless enabled.

3) Next steps: I'll loop in Marissa from Security to outline the feasible configurations (hosted with reduced retention vs Dedicated vs Private), and we'll provide SOC2 summary + data flow diagram. After that, we can put together a proposed DPA language and rough pricing delta for Dedicated/Private.

Proposed timeline: Marissa will follow up with technical options and constraints tomorrow; I can then schedule a 30-minute follow-up with our Solutions Engineer and your legal/procurement.

Thanks -- will be in touch with concrete options.

Best,

Hi all --

Following up with the technical options from Security/ProdInfra:

Option A -- Hosted (managed) with custom retention policy:
- We can configure account-level retention to purge stored request/response content after X days; minimum configurable retention = 7 days.
- Logs (audit/metrics) will still retain request IDs, timestamps, and non-content metadata for 90 days by default; we can reduce that to 30 days for an account-level setting.
- Note: Hosted with 0-content retention is operationally possible but carries tradeoffs: limited troubleshooting capability and reduced ability to investigate abuse incidents.

Option B -- Dedicated (reserved capacity)
- Deploy on dedicated GPU pool for Acme; persistent storage of request/response content can be disabled.
- Access controls: RBAC + customer SSO for console and API keys; we can restrict internal Redwood access to a narrow on-call list with cross-account auditing.
- Pricing: ~+25% on top of hosted rate (estimate) to cover reserved infra and additional compliance controls.

Option C -- Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Full control for Acme; data never leaves customer network if deployed on-prem. Redwood provides control plane optionally or a thin agent.
- Best fit for 0-retention and residency requirements.

Data handling specifics:
- Runtime ephemeral caches are not written to persistent logs.
- We can redact or hash specified fields (PII) at the ingestion layer - this requires work on your side to identify fields or supply a redaction mapping.
- We support CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) in Dedicated/Private for additional cryptographic controls.

Attachments: SOC2_summary.pdf and a simplified data_flow_diagram.png to show where data is stored and what is ephemeral.

If the customer is comfortable with a Hosted + 30-day logs + prompt/content purge policy, that is the lowest-friction path. If Acme requires zero retention for content, Dedicated or Private is the recommended path.

Happy to jump on a technical call Friday to run through options with your infra and security teams.

--Marissa
Marissa Cole
